faqs.q: Who do you act for?

faqs.q: Can you assess my case before I file a suit?
faqs.a: Yes. We review the relevant facts and documents, identify the available causes of action and remedies, and advise on the appropriate legal strategy before proceedings are commenced.

faqs.q: How long will a civil case take?
faqs.a: The duration depends on the nature and complexity of the dispute, the evidence involved, procedural developments and the court's schedule. We provide realistic guidance based on the circumstances of each matter.

faqs.q: Can a civil dispute be resolved without going to trial?
faqs.a: In appropriate cases, settlement, negotiation or other dispute-resolution mechanisms may provide a more efficient solution. We advise clients on the available options and their respective legal and commercial implications.

faqs.q: How are legal fees discussed?

services.title: Writ Appeals & Related Proceedings

faqs.q: When can a writ petition be filed?
faqs.a: A writ petition may be appropriate where a public authority or other entity exercising public functions has acted unlawfully, exceeded its jurisdiction, failed to perform a legal duty or infringed a legal or constitutional right. The availability of the remedy depends on the facts and applicable law.

faqs.q: Can a government decision be challenged through a writ?
faqs.a: Yes, in appropriate circumstances. Government and administrative decisions may be subject to judicial review where they are unlawful, made without jurisdiction, procedurally improper or otherwise amenable to constitutional review.

faqs.q: Can I file a writ against a private person or company?
faqs.a: Writ jurisdiction primarily concerns public authorities and the exercise of public functions. Whether a particular private entity or action falls within the scope of constitutional judicial review depends on the nature of the function and the applicable legal framework.

faqs.q: Can a writ petition stop an unlawful government action?
faqs.a: In appropriate cases, the High Court Division may grant interim or other appropriate relief to protect the petitioner's position while the matter is being considered. The availability and scope of such relief depend on the circumstances of each case.

faqs.q: Do I need to challenge the decision through another legal remedy first?
faqs.a: Not necessarily in every case. The maintainability of a writ petition may depend on the availability and adequacy of alternative remedies, the nature of the impugned action and other legal considerations. We assess these issues before recommending the appropriate course of action.

faqs.q: How are legal fees discussed?
faqs.a: Fees are discussed transparently after assessing the nature, complexity and scope of the matter. The proposed fee structure and professional engagement terms are communicated before commencement of the engagement.

faqs.q: Can I obtain interim relief during arbitration?

faqs.q: Can an arbitral award be challenged?

faqs.q: Can a foreign arbitral award be enforced in Bangladesh?

faqs.q: When should I consult a lawyer about a dispute?
faqs.a: Ideally, legal advice should be obtained as early as possible. Early assessment can help preserve evidence, identify available remedies, manage risks and determine whether litigation or another form of dispute resolution is appropriate.

faqs.q: Can you represent me throughout the entire litigation process?
faqs.a: Yes. We can assist from initial case assessment and pre-litigation strategy through pleadings, interim applications, trial, judgment, appeal and enforcement, depending on the nature of the matter.

faqs.q: Do all disputes need to go to trial?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. Depending on the circumstances, negotiation, mediation, arbitration or settlement may provide a more efficient resolution. We assess the dispute and advise on the most appropriate course of action.

faqs.q: Can I obtain an urgent court order before the case is decided?
faqs.a: In appropriate circumstances, interim or protective relief may be available to preserve rights or prevent irreparable harm while the dispute is pending. The availability of such relief depends on the facts and applicable law.

faqs.q: How do you assess the strength of a litigation case?
faqs.a: We consider the applicable law, facts, documentary and other evidence, procedural position, potential defences, available remedies and practical risks before advising on the prospects and appropriate litigation strategy.

faqs.q: Can you handle an appeal after a judgment?
faqs.a: Yes. We advise and represent clients in appropriate appellate and revisional proceedings and assess the available grounds, procedural requirements and prospects before pursuing an appeal or revision.

faqs.q: How are legal fees discussed?
faqs.a: Fees are discussed transparently after assessing the nature, complexity, value and scope of the dispute. The proposed fee structure and professional engagement terms are communicated before commencement of the engagement.
